title: Models Can Pass the Exam Without Knowing the Syllabus
hook: Educational benchmarks test whether a model answers school questions. This one tests whether it knows which concept comes before which — and the best model scores 57%.
key_points: The authors name the missing capability 'curriculum cognition': prerequisite chains, concept taxonomies, experiment links, pedagogical sequencing, visual grounding.
K12-KGraph is a knowledge graph extracted from official People's Education Press textbooks in maths, physics, chemistry, and biology.
K12-Bench derives 23,640 multi-select questions in five families: Ground, Prereq, Neighbor, Evidence, and Locate.
Gemini-3-Flash reaches only 57% exact match and Gemma-4-31B-IT 46%, with Prereq and Neighbor the hardest tasks.
At a matched 2,300-sample budget, its graph-guided training data beat equally sized subsets of eight mainstream instruction corpora on GaokaoBench and EduEval.
For vision-language models, combining text and visual supervision beat either alone — the two are complementary.
content_html: LLMs are already being used to teach children, but the benchmarks we judge them by mostly ask exam questions. Answering "what is the boiling point of water" correctly tells you nothing about whether the model knows that concept comes after states of matter and before distillation. The authors call that missing capability curriculum cognition.
extra_html:
Building the syllabus as a graph

K12-KGraph is extracted from official People's Education Press textbooks in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology, across primary, middle, and high school — nine node types and fourteen relation types covering prerequisite chains, concept taxonomies, experiment-concept links, pedagogical sequencing, and visual grounding in textbook figures. From the graph they derive K12-Bench, 23,640 multi-select questions in five task families: Ground, Prereq, Neighbor, Evidence, Locate.

Results

The scores are low for a school-level benchmark: Gemini-3-Flash manages 57% exact match, Gemma-4-31B-IT 46%, and the hardest families are Prereq and Neighbor — exactly the relational ones. The training half is arguably more interesting. Under a matched 2,300-sample budget, their graph-guided text corpus consistently outperformed equally sized subsets of eight mainstream instruction-tuning corpora on GaokaoBench and EduEval, and for vision-language models the combined text-plus-visual version beat both single-modality variants despite using fewer samples than larger baselines. Structure, not volume, did the work. Graph, benchmark, training data, and construction pipeline are all released. Liang and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: AI Tutors Jump In Too Soon
related.hook: Put an LLM in the tutor's seat and it interrupts sooner and more often than a human would — and hands over the whole solution where a person would have offered a hint.

related.title: Can We Trust Item Response Theory for AI Evaluation?
related.hook: IRT ranks models off a handful of items instead of averaging accuracy — but the math was built for human test-takers, and AI benchmarks break its assumptions in ways that quietly distort rankings.

related.title: The Pile: 800GB of Diverse Text
related.hook: Web text alone leaves gaps. The Pile stitches together 22 curated sources — academic and professional — so a language model picks up knowledge plain web crawls miss.

flashcards.prompt: What is 'curriculum cognition' and why isn't it covered by exam-QA benchmarks?
flashcards.back_html: Knowing how curriculum knowledge is structured — prerequisite chains, concept taxonomies, pedagogical sequencing, visual grounding. Answering a question correctly says nothing about knowing what must be taught before it.

flashcards.prompt: Which K12-Bench task families proved hardest for the models tested?

choices.text: Prereq and Neighbor — the tasks about relationships between concepts
Ground and Locate — the tasks requiring visual grounding in textbook figures
Evidence — linking experiments to the concepts they demonstrate

flashcards.explanation_html: The relational tasks are where models fall down, which fits the paper's thesis: they hold facts but not the curriculum's structure. Gemini-3-Flash managed 57% exact match overall.

flashcards.prompt: What did the matched-budget training comparison show?
flashcards.back_html: At 2,300 samples, graph-guided curriculum data consistently beat equally sized subsets of eight mainstream instruction-tuning corpora on GaokaoBench and EduEval — structure beat volume.
